intro: Three subordinating conjunctions that share one word order (verb at the end) and are constantly confused in meaning. wenn = when (repeatedly or in the future) or if: Wenn ich Zeit habe, lese ich; Wenn es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause. als = when, for a single event in the past: Als ich ein Kind war, wohnten wir in Köln; Als ich achtzehn wurde, … obwohl = although: Wir gehen spazieren, obwohl es kalt ist. The wenn/als split has no English equivalent — English 'when' covers both — and is one of the classic learner mistakes: past and once → als; anything repeated, present or future → wenn. Its cousin trotzdem (nevertheless) says the same as obwohl from the other side and is an adverb: verb second (Es ist kalt, trotzdem gehen wir spazieren). In the quiz there are no cues: the tense, a time word (gestern, letzten Sommer, immer) and the verb position tell you which word fits — including trotzdem, which keeps its verb second.
tips[0].title: als = once, in the past
tips[0].text: Als ich klein war, … Als wir in Rom waren, … Als ich das Abitur machte, … One event or one period, finished. Present tense or repetition → never als.
tips[0].trap: 'When I was a child' = Als ich ein Kind war. 'Wenn ich ein Kind war' means 'whenever I was a child' — nonsense in German.
tips[0].check.why: gestern makes it one single event in the past, so the conjunction is als. wann only asks questions.
tips[0].visual.caption: als: one moment in the past. wenn: every time, or in the future.
tips[0].visual.marks[0].label: once, in the past
tips[0].visual.marks[1].label: every time (past)
tips[0].visual.marks[2].label: future
tips[1].title: wenn = whenever, or if, or future when
tips[1].text: Wenn es regnet, … (every time / if). Wenn ich fertig bin, rufe ich an (future). Immer wenn … (whenever). Also for repeated past: Wenn wir in Rom waren, haben wir immer Eis gegessen.
tips[1].check.why: Immer wenn = whenever: a repeated situation in the present always takes wenn.
tips[2].title: obwohl (verb last) = trotzdem (verb second)
tips[2].text: Obwohl es kalt ist, gehen wir spazieren. = Es ist kalt, trotzdem gehen wir spazieren. Same meaning, opposite grammar — like weil/deshalb, which you already know.
tips[2].check.why: The verb gehen comes straight after the gap, in second position, so you need the adverb trotzdem. obwohl would send the verb to the end.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].a: Obwohl es regnet, gehe ich spazieren.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].b: Es regnet. Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.
tips[3].title: als = a single snapshot
tips[3].text: Picture a single photo: als. A film running on a loop, or a plan: wenn. If you can add 'every time' or 'if', it's wenn.
tips[3].check.why: One film, one evening, finished: a single snapshot in the past takes als.
remember[0]: Past + once → als. Everything else → wenn.
remember[1]: obwohl kicks the verb; trotzdem keeps it second.
mistakes[0].why: A single past period takes als.
mistakes[2].why: After a fronted subordinate clause, the main verb comes first.
hook: German splits English “when” in two: als for one moment in the past, wenn for everything else. Plus obwohl for “although”.
